title: Neutralisation & salts
examples: What happens when an acid mixes with a base?
How do I write the chemical equation for neutralisation?
What do I call the product when an acid and a base react?

explain.say: Today we learn about neutralisation reactions in chemistry.
When an acid reacts with a base, it forms a salt and water.
If we mix hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide, we get sodium chloride and water.
An acid reacting with a carbonate produces a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas.
When an acid reacts with a metal, it produces a salt and hydrogen gas.
In real life, antacids are used to neutralise excess stomach acid.

faq.q: What is the general name for the salt produced?
faq.a: The salt is formed from the cation of the base and the anion of the acid.
asks: What do I name the product?

faq.q: Does the reaction always produce water?
faq.a: Yes, in a standard neutralisation, water is always one of the products.
asks: Must water be in the equation?

faq.q: What do I do if the acid is in the gas state?
faq.a: You must write the full chemical formula for the gas acid involved.
asks: What if the acid is a gas?
Do I change the formula for gases?

faq.q: When a carbonate reacts, is the gas always carbon dioxide?
faq.a: Yes, carbonates always produce carbon dioxide gas when reacting with an acid.

faq.q: Can a metal react with an acid if it is coated?
faq.a: The reaction will only happen if the acid can reach the bare metal surface.

facts: Neutralisation reactions occur between an acid and a base.
The products of a neutralisation are always a salt and water.
When a carbonate reacts with an acid, carbon dioxide gas is released.
When a metal reacts with an acid, hydrogen gas is produced.

quiz.say: What are the two main reactants in a neutralisation?
quiz.why: The definition of neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base.

wrong.0: This reaction produces carbon dioxide, not just water.
wrong.1: This combination does not typically result in neutralisation.
wrong.2: These are products, not the starting reactants.

quiz.say: If nitric acid reacts with magnesium, what gas is formed?
quiz.why: When a metal reacts with an acid, hydrogen gas is the gas produced.

wrong.0: Nitrogen gas is generally produced by other specific reactions.
wrong.2: This gas comes from reacting with carbonates.
wrong.3: Oxygen gas is usually involved in combustion reactions.

quiz.say: Write the equation for potassium hydroxide reacting with hydrochloric acid.
quiz.why: Potassium hydroxide is the base, and hydrochloric acid is the acid; the salt is potassium chloride.

wrong.0: The stoichiometry must balance the potassium and chloride ions correctly.
wrong.2: The salt must be formed by combining the metal/ammonium from the base and the anion from the acid.
wrong.3: Carbon dioxide is only produced when a carbonate is involved.
